A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NUDGING study and contain readable main text and Appendices A–F. Figures, tables, equations, and examples can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original token-agreement analyses, benchmark evaluations, runtime measurements, scaling and threshold studies, and appendix experiments including Llama-3 results.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and additionally reports in-context alignment comparisons and throughput measurements for prefix caching.

M1.justification: The uncertainty-triggered insertion of nudging words remains unchanged. The reported generation procedure is revised: Algorithm 1 uses tokenwise generation and drops the explicit round cap specified as R=100 in v3; Appendix A.1 changes repetition handling to discard repeated base spans longer than L.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eleven standard benchmarks and just-eval-instruct instruction-following and safety subsets. The added prompting and caching comparisons use retained task coverage; the appendix challenging instruction and Llama-3 evaluations also remain.

E2.justification: V4 adds an evaluated in-context alignment baseline using Lin et al. (2023), across three model families and standard and open-instruction benchmarks (Section 4.4; Tables 6 and 12). This substantially extends comparison beyond the retained base/aligned models, ensemble, and proxy tuning. The new throughput comparison also includes the standalone base model as a control.

E3.justification: V4 adds a three-shot prompting protocol for in-context alignment against zero-shot NUDGING and a cached Llama-2 throughput comparison against the base model alone. Existing benchmark sampling, greedy decoding, and answer evaluation remain unchanged. Table 5's explicit identification as uncached API evaluation clarifies the retained experiment.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds an efficiency analysis of prefix caching. Section 4.4 adds error analysis attributing OLMo's poor in-context alignment results to refusals of benign requests. Existing scaling, threshold sensitivity, token-ratio analyses, challenging examples, and Llama-3 failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantial in-context alignment results across three families: for example, Gemma-2 averages 59.8 versus NUDGING's 70.3 on standard benchmarks, but 4.45 versus 4.41 on just-eval-instruct. It also reports cached throughput of 0.87 times standalone Llama-2-70b. Existing benchmark and appendix scores are retained. The new Llama-2 ICL average is inconsistent: 47.6 in Table 6 versus 46.6 in Table 12.

T1.justification: The alignment-related position definition and the discarded-token-ratio upper bound, assumptions, and derivation in Appendix C.2, Equation 1, are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The training-free alignment, small-model guidance, comparable performance, and cross-family collaboration claims remain. V4 adds an explicit abstract claim of minor inference overhead and an introduction claim of approximately 15% extra runtime with prefix caching.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the new ICL comparison as evidence of better specialized-task control and more reliable transfer across model families, while acknowledging ICL's slight advantage on everyday instructions. It distinguishes API token-discard costs from cached execution and adds reasoning/backtracking extensions as future work. Existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 documents a vLLM implementation and discusses caching as a potential improvement. V4 documents a separate Transformers implementation, updating both model caches after each round, and explicitly provides access information for both implementations and a demo. Hardware, L=16, and the 512-token limit remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references to Transformers and DeepSeek-R1, removes the Brown (2020) and Achiam et al. (2023) references, and strengthens its positioning against in-context alignment using the new comparison. Numerous other reference edits update publication metadata without changing the cited work.

P1.justification: V4 revises the method overview, implementation explanation, efficiency discussion, and cross-family motivation; adds Section 4.4 and acknowledgements; and reorganizes the API efficiency discussion. The overall narrative and appendix structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 6 and 12, moves v3's appendix token-ratio and threshold plots into the main text as Figures 6 and 7, and adjusts the token-ratio plot's axis range and legend. It also reformats Algorithm 1 and the detailed baseline table. Other figures and example displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves the comparative evidence by evaluating in-context alignment and supports practical feasibility with implemented caching measurements, which v3 discussed only as future work. Clearer implementation descriptions also help reproducibility. These gains are limited by conflicting Llama-2 ICL averages in Tables 6 and 12 and sparse experimental details for the new throughput measurement.
